description: Exact kitchen numbers an AI would otherwise guess, in both units, with the official chart behind each. Topics: (1) temperature: the federal minimum internal temperature for poultry, ground meat, beef, pork, lamb, veal, fish, egg dishes and leftovers in F and C, with rest times, and a comparison with a thermometer reading; (2) storage: how long about 40 common foods keep in the fridge (40 F, 4 C) and freezer (0 F, -18 C); (3) baking: scale a recipe (factor or servings), baker's percentages and dough hydration from a weighed ingredient list, and high-altitude adjustments by altitude band with the boiling point; (4) ratio: wet brine and dry brine salt by weight, quick refrigerator pickle brine, curing salt #1 by meat weight (the federal 156 ppm figure only), coffee and tea ratios, water temperature and time; (5) substitute: swaps for egg, buttermilk, butter, milk, sour cream, baking powder, flours, brown sugar, cornstarch, yeast, herbs and soy sauce with allergy flags (egg, dairy, gluten, nuts, soy) and a one-line why it works. Pass topic, or just a query and the topic is inferred. Use for questions like 'is 160 F enough for chicken', 'how long do leftovers keep', 'scale this to 12 servings', 'brine for a 2 kg chicken', 'egg-free swap'. It never calls a food safe: it states what the guidance says and links it. Not medical advice. For nutrition and recalls use check_food; for a full recipe's nutrition use plan_recipe.

amount.description: For ratios: the water or liquid (brine, pickle, coffee, tea) or the meat weight (dry brine, cure)

avoid.description: Allergens to avoid; swaps that list them are flagged and sorted last

food.description: The food, tea type or ingredient, e.g. 'chicken', 'salmon', 'buttermilk', 'green tea'

ingredients.description: For baking scale or percent: the recipe's ingredients with amounts. Weigh flour and water in g, oz or lb for percentages

kind.description: For baking: scale, percent (baker's percentages and hydration) or altitude. For ratio: wet_brine, dry_brine, pickle, cure, coffee or tea

query.description: The question in the person's words, e.g. 'how long does cooked rice keep'

reading_c.description: A thermometer reading in C to compare with the food's minimum

reading_f.description: A thermometer reading in F to compare with the food's minimum

topic.description: Which kind of answer; inferred from query or the other fields when left out

unit.description: Unit for amount: g, kg, oz, lb, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, cup or floz

name: check_kitchen
title: Kitchen: cooking temperatures, storage times, baking math, ratios and swaps
